name: Anomalous Coronary Arteries

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical presentation

criteria.description: Coronary artery originating from an abnormal sinus of Valsalva or inappropriate location
Coronary artery coursing between the aorta and pulmonary artery (interarterial course)
Clinical evidence of myocardial ischemia or sudden cardiac arrest unexplained by other causes
Confirmation of anomalous coronary anatomy by coronary angiography, CT angiography, or MRI
Exclusion of other causes of ischemia or sudden cardiac death

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of anomalous coronary artery origin or course on imaging with or without ischemic symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities; clinical presentation varies widely.

pathognomonic.notes: Often due to transient ischemia during exertion
May be first manifestation, especially in young athletes

common.notes: Chest pain due to myocardial ischemia
Secondary to cardiac ischemia or dysfunction

laboratory: Generally normal cardiac biomarkers unless acute ischemia or infarction present
imaging: Coronary CT angiography showing anomalous coronary artery origin or course
Invasive coronary angiography confirming abnormal coronary anatomy
Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial ischemia or fibrosis
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; congenital etiology
other: Exercise stress testing may provoke ischemic changes or arrhythmias
Electrocardiogram may show ischemic changes or arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of atherosclerotic plaques on imaging
Genetic testing positive for sarcomeric mutations

redFlags: Sudden cardiac arrest during or immediately after exertion
Unexplained angina in young individuals without risk factors
references: Taylor AJ, Rogan KM, Virmani R. Sudden cardiac death associated with isolated congenital coronary artery anomalies. J Am Coll Cardiol. 1992;20(3):640-647.
Cheezum MK, Liberthson RR, Shah NR, et al. Anomalous coronary arteries: diagnosis and management. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2017;69(12):1592-1608.

Brothers JA, Frommelt MA, Jaquiss RD, Myerburg RJ, Fraser CD Jr, Tweddell JS. Expert consensus guidelines: Anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery. J Thorac Cardiovasc Surg. 2017;153(6):1440-1457.
